evidence.excerpt:
As preferences, goals, and facts change, LLM agents must use the current state
while earlier versions remain in context. Yet they can answer with an old value
of the same variable, a failure that we callstale binding. To study when models
use outdated information and why, we introduce Controlled In-Context Memory
(CICM), a benchmark for tracking and using updated information in conversations
and agent logs. We observe that even frontier reasoning models can fail to recover
the current state. We find that in open-source models probes can still recover the
updated value when the model answers with an old one, pointing to a failure to
select information that remains available. Component tests in Qwen and Pythia
identify a mechanism for this selection failure: attention drift, where attention
favors old values over the current one when producing an answer. We study a
one-layer transformer

When a model returns an old value, one possible explanation is that it has lost the current value from
its internal representation. However, a linear probe can still recover information about the current
value from the model's hidden state, even when its answer is incorrect. On old-value errors, a linear
probe assigns the current value a mean probability of 84.8% in Qwen and 82.2% in Llama, against
3.2–6.4% when the value labels are randomly reassigned (Figure 5a). Other-variable errors show
similar recoverability (Appendix Table 6). The probe reads the standardized final-layer hidden state

A shift in attention on failures is still a correlation. By replacing components we can causally test
whether they produce the answer.
Attention selects positions through query–key matching and transmits their information through
value vectors and the output projection (Vaswani et al., 2017). For 120 failed synthetic overwrite
prompts, we construct successful counterparts with identical candidate values and positions, renaming
earlier assignments to remove competition for the queried variable (Appendix B.6). We then replace
components in failed runs with their successful counterparts (Qwen rows in Table 1). Recovery
concentrates in late hidden states and old-value keys, implicating late selection and competing keys.

correct. Across the five adaptive configurations, absolute accuracy gains range from 44.79 to 78.75%,
with 98.08 to 100% of initially correct answers preserved (Table 2). These improvements depend on
which positions and heads are targeted: all five gains exceed the observed ranges of random-head
and random-position

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Routing heads and bias settings were calibrated on separate discovery and validation splits, and final efficacy was measured on held-out test dialogues using programmatic value matching against random-position, random-head, and reverse-routing controls.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out test accuracy and old-error correction counts scored by fixed programmatic value matching.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Gradient sensitivity of the current-minus-old answer score and calibration failed-minus-correct attention differences used to select heads and routing hyperparameters.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are strongly supported by the evidence and carefully qualified; the authors explicitly distinguish between recoverable information and actual selection, show model-specific nuances (e.g., attention differences detected in Qwen but not Llama), and document edge cases where intervention does not fully correct errors.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations span open-weight models (Qwen, Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Pythia) and proprietary frontier models (GPT-4o, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8). The experimental setup incorporates comprehensive ablation controls (random-head, random-position, reverse-routing, and paired linearized controls) and rigorous uncertainty quantification using bootstrapped intervals.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final routing efficacy was corroborated on strictly held-out test splits evaluated via programmatic value matching against random-position, random-head, and reverse-routing baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Accuracy and error-category persistence on held-out evaluation dialogues evaluated via exact programmatic keyword/state-replay matching.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Heads and routing hyperparameter bias values were calibrated on designated training/discovery splits using gradient sensitivity of the answer margin or calibration failed-minus-correct attention differences.

primary.limitations: The manuscript acknowledges limitations clearly, noting that synthetic/controlled logs may not fully mirror wild agent traces, that probe recoverability does not imply native utilization, and that attention routing requires white-box model access, calibrated heads, and structured parsing.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is rigorous and well-controlled, incorporating linear probing against shuffled-label baselines, causal component replacement and head knockouts on held-out pairs, and test-time attention biasing. Benchmark tasks across dialogues, constraint decisions, and long operational histories feature deterministic state checks, programmatic replay validation, and matched snapshot controls.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers exceptional depth, providing clear definitions, thorough mechanistic analyses, formal theoretical bounds on RoPE attention under multiple updates, and robust empirical validation across several model architectures with strict controls.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper characterizes 'stale binding' update errors where LLMs output outdated values of an updated variable despite full context availability. It introduces the Controlled In-Context Memory (CICM) benchmark, investigates internal representations via probing and causal interventions (identifying attention drift), provides a one-layer RoPE theoretical model, and demonstrates training-free test-time attention routing to mitigate these errors.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers exceptional depth, providing clear definitions, thorough mechanistic analyses, formal theoretical bounds on RoPE attention under multiple updates, and robust empirical validation across several model architectures with strict controls.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript acknowledges limitations clearly, noting that synthetic/controlled logs may not fully mirror wild agent traces, that probe recoverability does not imply native utilization, and that attention routing requires white-box model access, calibrated heads, and structured parsing.
